title: The Prisoner's Dilemma
description: You're in a series of negotiations with an unknown partner. Each round: do you cooperate for mutual gain, or defect for personal advantage? Your partner adapts to your strategy.
coaching_moment: The Prisoner's Dilemma teaches the most important lesson in game theory: mutual cooperation produces better outcomes than mutual defection — but only when both players trust each other. Building that trust is the real game.

rounds.title: Round 1: First Move
rounds.scenario: Round 1 of 7. Your partner is unknown. If you both Cooperate: +3 each. If you Defect and they Cooperate: +5 for you, 0 for them. If both Defect: +1 each. If you Cooperate and they Defect: 0 for you, +5 for them.

choices.label: Cooperate — signal trust from the start
choices.outcome: Partner cooperates (Round 1: they always cooperate). Both gain +3. Trust established.

choices.label: Defect — maximize first-round gain
choices.outcome: Partner cooperates. You gain +5, they gain 0. Trust damaged from the start.

rounds.coaching_moment: The first move sets the tone. Cooperation signals willingness to build a relationship. Defection signals self-interest. Your partner is watching.

expert_pick.reason: Ethical decision-making builds lasting trust — the foundation of all leadership.

rounds.title: Round 2: Response
rounds.scenario: Round 2. Your partner mirrors your last move (tit-for-tat strategy). What do you do?

choices.label: Cooperate — maintain the relationship
choices.outcome: Partner cooperates (if you cooperated last round) or defects (if you defected). Outcome depends on your Round 1 choice.

choices.label: Defect — take the advantage again
choices.outcome: Your partner mirrors your last move. If you were cooperative, this betrayal costs both heavily.

rounds.coaching_moment: Tit-for-tat is a powerful strategy because it rewards cooperation and punishes defection — symmetrically. It's not revenge; it's feedback.

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Round 3: The Test
rounds.scenario: Round 3 of 7. You're halfway through the early game. Your score depends on the pattern so far.

choices.label: Cooperate — stay consistent
choices.outcome: Consistent cooperation builds the highest long-term scores when partner mirrors you.

choices.label: Defect — try to gain an edge
choices.outcome: If partner mirrors you, defecting now triggers retaliatory defection for remaining rounds.

rounds.coaching_moment: Consistency is a trust signal. Unpredictable partners are treated as threats. Predictably cooperative partners are treated as allies.

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Round 4: Midpoint
rounds.scenario: Midgame. If you've been cooperating, you're both doing well. If defection has occurred, both are likely stuck in mutual defection. Can you reset?

choices.label: Cooperate — signal intent to reset even after defection
choices.outcome: Generous tit-for-tat: one-time forgiveness. Partner may reset cooperation if trust wasn't fully destroyed.

choices.label: Defect — locked in mutual defection now
choices.outcome: Both players stuck in +1/+1 per round. Far from optimal.

rounds.coaching_moment: Recovery from betrayal is possible, but it requires one player to take the cooperative risk first. That takes courage and long-term thinking.

expert_pick.reason: Ethical decision-making builds lasting trust — the foundation of all leadership.

rounds.title: Round 5: Endgame Temptation
rounds.scenario: 3 rounds left. Game theory predicts rational defection increases near the end. Your partner knows this. Do you defect early?

choices.label: Cooperate — reject the endgame logic
choices.outcome: If both players reject endgame defection, both earn 3/round more than if they defected. Long-term thinking wins.

choices.label: Defect — rational endgame strategy
choices.outcome: If partner anticipates this, they also defect. Both end up with +1/round for remaining rounds.

rounds.coaching_moment: The endgame defection trap is a self-fulfilling prophecy. Leaders who build cultures of trust learn to override the rational defection impulse.

expert_pick.reason: Ethical decision-making builds lasting trust — the foundation of all leadership.

rounds.title: Round 6: Second-to-Last
rounds.scenario: One round after this. Defection is now statistically 'optimal' for rational actors. But you've built something.

choices.label: Cooperate — honor the relationship to the end
choices.outcome: Final trust signal. If partner also cooperates, you both end with the highest possible scores.

choices.label: Defect — secure final advantage
choices.outcome: Short-term gain, long-term regret. The relationship ends with betrayal.

rounds.coaching_moment: Honoring a relationship when it's no longer 'economically rational' is the definition of integrity. Others remember how you acted when you didn't have to be good.

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Final Round
rounds.scenario: Last round. Your final move defines your legacy in this game. Cooperate for mutual gain, or defect for individual maximum?

choices.label: Cooperate — end with integrity
choices.outcome: If partner cooperates: both earn +3. Together you've maximized mutual gain across 7 rounds. This is the Nash cooperative equilibrium.

choices.label: Defect — take the final prize
choices.outcome: You gain +5, partner gains 0. But your total cooperation score is lower than if you'd cooperated all 7 rounds.

rounds.coaching_moment: The prisoner's dilemma proves that ethical behavior and strategic behavior are not opposites — they converge in repeated games. Integrity is not just right; it's optimal.

expert_pick.reason: Ethical decision-making builds lasting trust — the foundation of all leadership.

reflection_prompt: In the Prisoner's Dilemma, did you cooperate or defect more? What does your pattern reveal about how you approach trust in real relationships?
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through rounds gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
